pages.text: Evening. The room smells of tea. Minena has brought a cup and spilled half of it. The others sit on the floor, on the bed, on your feet.
“Tell us about the farm that burned down!” “Again?” you say. “Yes!” “And don't forget the bells,” whispers someone very small. “Shh! That comes later!”
You close your eyes. You are not sure you remember it right. But it always begins the same way: with ash.
Everything is grey. Ash, mud, black posts where a house once stood. The farm of your family is gone.
But look. One green patch in the ash. On it stands one ripe wheat stalk. Every grain has been nibbled off. All but one.
You pick up the last grain. Somebody was here. And somebody left it for you.
The book in the box is old. On the first page, in thin brown ink: “Start small. Small is plenty.”
You read it twice. Then, from nowhere, an old tune comes back, and a line of words: “Long ears sow the clover green.”
The first night. The sky is huge, and so full of stars that the dark between them looks crowded. At the edge of the forest, a line of white stones glows, very faintly.

Somewhere, a tune: a few slow notes, going up and turning round. You find you are humming it. The stones get a little brighter. You stop and stand still, and they stay bright, until you shift your feet.

c1_bells.title: A little bell
c1_bells.text: When the last thistle is out, you hear it: a tiny bell, high in the air. Then nothing. Behind you, three sticks lie in a very silly pile. Nothing is missing.

c1_ledger.title: A burnt page
c1_ledger.text: Under the black boards you find a page, burnt at the edges. At the bottom, in red: “The Lord's share.” One sack in ten. Then one in five. Then one in three. Then one in two, circled so hard the pen went through. You fold the page small, and then smaller, and keep it.

pages.text: On the track by your field a seller sniffs the air. “Is that porridge?” You hand her a bowl. She eats it standing up, very fast.
“You're from Moonedge, aren't you?” she says. “Good porridge, {player}. I'll tell everyone that somebody is cooking up here again.”

c1_board.title: The notice board
c1_board.text: A notice board, full of little papers. Somebody needs a basket mended. Somebody has a pig for sale: “a good pig, a talker.” Somebody has lost a green glove, left hand. You read every paper twice, with your hat pulled low, because reading is something you can do without anyone talking to you.

pages.text: A bunny sits on the one green patch. She is small and brown, and one ear will not stand up. She sits as if the whole patch was built round her, and she eats your carrot with great concentration and no thanks.
Now you understand. The patch stayed green because somebody looked after it. The stalk was nibbled because somebody was hungry. And one grain was left for you.

The bunny was Moonedge's, once. You remember now, the way you remember a dream: a brown back in a basket, a nose against your hand. “Long ears sow the clover green,” you say, and the crooked ear twitches. You wait for the next line. Nothing comes.

c1_bell_out.title: Two soft rings
c1_bell_out.text: That night, from far away: two soft rings of a very small bell. You sit up in the dark. The bunny is asleep in the clover. So who else is still here?

pages.text: Back in the room, the tea has gone cold. “Was there really a bunny?” asks Minena. “There was,” you say. “She was very rude about carrots.”
“And the bell? Who rang the bell?” “Shh!” says everybody at once. “That's next time!” You smile. They know this story almost as well as you do. Almost.

c1_k_seller.text: “Do you ever stop?” calls a cart driver from the track. You wave. You do not stop.

c1_k_hens.text: The hens argue about who laid which egg. Nobody wins.

c1_k_bucket.text: The old bucket clanks against the well stones. It sounds almost proud.

c1_k_grass.text: Something rustles in the long grass. It stops when you look.

c1_k_smoke.text: The wind still smells a little of old smoke.

c1_k_winter.text: The tent flaps in the wind. You pull the blanket up to your nose.

c1_k_hen_alone.text: Your one hen walks round the coop twice, looking for someone to argue with. There is nobody. She argues with a stone.

c1_k_eggs.text: So many eggs. You line them up on a plank. One rolls into the straw, on purpose, you are sure of it.

c1_k_tall_weeds.text: The weeds on one patch reach over your boots now. A beetle sits right on top and enjoys the view.

c1_k_yawn.text: You yawn so wide that a passing fly changes its mind.

c1_k_dry_bucket.text: You tip the bucket upside down. One drop falls out, very slowly, as if it is sorry.

c1_k_rain.text: It rains. The field drinks and drinks and does not say thank you. Fields never do.

c1_k_caterpillar.text: A caterpillar sits on a leaf in your field, chewing. It has a very good plan and no manners at all.

c1_k_worm.text: Some patches lie bare. A worm pokes its head out, looks around, and goes back down to wait for seeds.
